lessonPlan.topic: Student Book  p.22 - A Look & Learn

details: Look and learn introduces the difference between -ing and -ed adjectives, building awareness of how we describe things and how we describe people’s feelings about experiences.
Look for correct identification of which adjectives describe a thing and which describe a feeling, giving simple examples.

“So have you decided? Shall we go to Fairy Land Amusement Park? I think I want to! I’m excited. The attractions are exciting. What do you think? Can you tell me how something is, and how you feel? Let’s see!”

Heads Up: 
Focus the students’ attention on the CPT and present relevant features of the language (MFP). Then demonstrate the activity with TA/students.
Heads Down: 
Ss open their books. Instruct and ask ICQs. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Heads Together: 
Demo/Instruct and ask ICQs, including setting behaviour expectations. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Reward moment
Check behaviour expectations and reward with APOS or remind for 4Rs

lessonPlan.topic: Student Book  p.22 - B Choose & complete

details: Choose and complete the sentences gives controlled practice with -ing / -ed adjective pairs, helping students choose the correct form to describe subjects and people’s feelings in short sentences.
Look for correct choices in each pair, clear and legible spelling, and students reading their completed sentences aloud using the correct adjective form.
“I’m still not sure how something is… and how I feel! I really need your help to complete the sentences. How fast can we do it together? Let’s go!”

lessonPlan.topic: Student Book  p.22 - C Complete the dialogues

details: Complete the dialogues practises -ing and -ed adjectives in short conversations, preparing students to talk more naturally about events and feelings.
Look for correct adjective forms in the gaps, dialogues that make clear sense, and pairs reading the mini-dialogues with understandable pronunciation and intonation.
“OK! I think I understand now… but I want to try with some new words. Let’s write them in each sentence. Then I’m ready to tell everyone all about my favourite thing - amusement parks!!”
